A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same PunchBench benchmark and SC-CoQ method. The complete documents, including Appendices A–F, are readable and support matching text, tables, figures, and renumbered material. One poorly explained chart creates localized interpretive uncertainty.

before.justification: v1 reports original PunchBench evaluations of six MLLMs and human performance in Table 1, caption-perturbation experiments, and human pairwise evaluations in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and expands Table 1 with additional model families and configurations.

M1.justification: Benchmark construction and both intra-task and inter-task SC-CoQ procedures remain unchanged. Section 4, Appendix B, and the corresponding prompt figures retain the same question sequences and response conditioning.

E1.justification: The explicitly described coverage remains 6,000 image-caption pairs, 54,000 questions, four domains, and the same perception and reasoning tasks. However, removed v1 Figure 6 includes undefined SQA/MQA series; the PDFs do not establish whether these represent distinct task requirements or settings within retained coverage. The newly mentioned validation set has no separately reported evaluation.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated comparisons using LLaVA-OneVision, InternVL2.5, MiniCPM-o 2.6, and Aria across both tasks and all prompting conditions, substantially broadening the model comparison. The original models, human baseline, zero-shot, CoT, and 3-shot comparators remain.

E3.justification: Table 1 adds 2B and 72B Qwen2-VL configurations alongside the retained 7B model. Table 2 specifies greedy decoding for the four added model families. Existing metrics, automatic evaluator, prompting conditions, human sampling procedures, and original models' decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The documented caption-sensitivity experiments, human-evaluation analysis, and qualitative cases are retained. v1 Figure 6 is removed, but its caption describes synonymous/antonymous captions while its legend mixes question formats with undefined SQA/MQA series. This prevents determining whether a distinct supplementary analysis was removed.

E5.justification: Both Table 1 captions report averages over four replicates and p-values below 0.01. Appendix D retains the same human-agreement procedure and Gwet's gamma reporting in Table 3. No additional uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds 144 accuracy entries for six additional model configurations; all original model scores remain unchanged. SC-CoQ leads every added comparison. New results include Qwen2-VL-72B scoring 48.8 versus GPT-4V's retained 48.1 on zero-shot perception Multi-choice QA. These are additional configuration results, not improvements to an unchanged model. The SQA/MQA entries in v1 Figure 6 also disappear.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 retains the same definitions of image-caption pairs, caption variants, and labels. Neither version adds formal propositions, proofs, or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: reducing caption shortcuts, providing diverse punchline evaluation, demonstrating a human–MLLM gap, and improving performance through SC-CoQ. The resource-release statement adds access information without redefining the scientific claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning question difficulty, caption shortcuts, and SC-CoQ's benefits remain unchanged. Both versions retain the static-image limitation and proposed extension to video. Section 5.3 also retains its broad closed-source-superiority statement despite the expanded results.

D1.justification: v1 promises a dataset release and supplies an anonymous preview site; v2 reports a public code-and-data repository. Appendix E specifies release without benchmark answers alongside a labeled validation set. This substantially changes the reported reproducibility resources. Appendix C additionally documents the new models' backbones and decoding settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for the newly evaluated models and their components, alongside additional humor, video-model, and evaluation literature. Section 2 and the positioning against previous punchline benchmarks remain substantively unchanged. Duplicate Qwen-VL and Qwen2 bibliography entries do not represent new research works.

P1.justification: v2 updates author affiliations and contact information, adds acknowledgements and release wording, and expands the model descriptions. Most prose and the main section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains rows and uses more compact typesetting, while Table 2 expands with decoding rows. v1 Figure 6 is removed; its Figures 7–26 are retained as v2 Figures 6–25. Several appendix tables and figures move, but their designs and the overall two-column layout remain substantially intact.

improvement.justification: The expanded model and size comparisons provide broader evidence for SC-CoQ, while reported public resources and additional configuration details improve reuse. Some interpretation remains insufficiently updated: Section 5.3 claims consistent closed-source superiority although Qwen2-VL-72B exceeds GPT-4V in several new comparisons. Removing Figure 6 also loses poorly explained scores, while the documented sensitivity and human checks remain. Overall, the revision provides a limited net quality improvement.
